blocks.text: 94 תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 94
uncertainties: The header is small and partly cut off at the top of band 1. The pointing comes from the full image.

blocks.text: תִּכְרַע כָּל־בֶּֽרֶךְ תִּשָּׁבַע כָּל־לָשׁוֹן׃ לְפָנֶֽיךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ יִכְרְעוּ וְיִפּֽוֹלוּ. וְלִכְבוֹד שִׁמְךָ יְקָר יִתֵּֽנוּ. וִיקַבְּלוּ כֻלָּם אֶת־עֹל מַלְכוּתֶֽךָ. וְתִמְלוֹךְ עֲלֵיהֶם מְהֵרָה לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. כִּי הַמַּלְכוּת שֶׁלְּךָ הִיא וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עַד תִּמְלוֹךְ בְּכָבוֹד׃ כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶֽךָ.
uncertainties: This passage continues from the previous page (it starts mid-Aleinu).

The marks under the stressed syllables (meteg, ֽ) in בֶּֽרֶךְ, לְפָנֶֽיךָ, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ, וְיִפּֽוֹלוּ, יִתֵּֽנוּ, מַלְכוּתֶֽךָ and בְּתוֹרָתֶֽךָ are small. They might instead be a different accent, or in some cases missing.
I can't tell whether the first letter of כֻלָּם has a dagesh.
The holam on the divine name is faint. The vowels shown are sheva and qamats, and there may be a holam dot. This is written out in full (יהוה), unlike the יְיָ used elsewhere on the page.
לְעֹלָם is spelled without the vav (defective), as in the image.

blocks.text: וְנֶאֱמַר לֹא הִבִּיט אָוֶן בְּיַעֲקֹב וְלֹא רָאָה עָמָל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יְיָ אֱלֹהָיו עִמּוֹ וּתְרוּעַת מֶלֶךְ בּוֹ׃
uncertainties: This block starts a new paragraph with an indent. וְנֶאֱמַר is the introductory formula.

blocks.text: וְנֶאֱמַר וַיְהִי בִישֻׁרוּן מֶלֶךְ בְּהִתְאַסֵּף רָאשֵׁי עָם יַחַד שִׁבְטֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
uncertainties: There may be a small accent under יַחַד. In בִישֻׁרוּן I see no dagesh in the bet.

blocks.text: וּבְדִבְרֵי קָדְשְׁךָ כָּתוּב לֵאמֹר כִּי לַייָ הַמְּלוּכָה וּמוֹשֵׁל בַּגּוֹיִם׃
uncertainties: There may be a meteg on קָדְשְׁךָ (קָֽדְשְׁךָ).

blocks.text: וְנֶאֱמַר יְיָ מָלָךְ גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ לָבֵשׁ יְיָ עֹז הִתְאַזָּר אַף תִּכּוֹן תֵּבֵל בַּל תִּמּוֹט׃
uncertainties: The image has no maqaf in בַּל תִּמּוֹט. עֹז is written without the vav.

blocks.text: וְנֶאֱמַר שְׂאוּ שְׁעָרִים רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְהִנָּשְׂאוּ פִּתְחֵי עוֹלָם וְיָבוֹא מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד׃ מִי זֶה מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד יְיָ עִזּוּז וְגִבּוֹר יְיָ גִּבּוֹר מִלְחָמָה׃ שְׂאוּ שְׁעָרִים רָאשֵׁיכֶם וּשְׂאוּ פִּתְחֵי עוֹלָם וְיָבוֹא מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד׃ מִי הוּא זֶה מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד יְיָ צְבָאוֹת הוּא מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד סֶלָה׃
uncertainties: The image spells וְיָבוֹא with the vav both times (plene). That doesn't match the Masoretic spelling in verse 9.
I'm not certain of the dagesh marks in עִזּוּז.

blocks.text: וְעַל יְדֵי עֲבָדֶֽיךָ הַנְּבִיאִים כָּתוּב לֵאמֹר כֹּה אָמַר יְיָ מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגֹאֲלוֹ יְיָ צְבָאוֹת אֲנִי רִאשׁוֹן וַאֲנִי אַחֲרוֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדַי אֵין אֱלֹהִים׃
uncertainties: The meteg in עֲבָדֶֽיךָ is uncertain.

blocks.text: וְנֶאֱמַר וְעָלוּ מוֹשִׁיעִים בְּהַר צִיּוֹן לִשְׁפֹּט אֶת הַר עֵשָׂו וְהָיְתָה לַייָ הַמְּלוּכָה׃
uncertainties: The image has מוֹשִׁיעִים with a yod (plene). The Masoretic text spells it without one.
There is no maqaf in אֶת הַר.

blocks.text: וְנֶאֱמַר וְהָיָה יְיָ לְמֶֽלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאָֽרֶץ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד׃
uncertainties: The metegs in לְמֶֽלֶךְ and הָאָֽרֶץ are uncertain. There is no maqaf in כָּל הָאָרֶץ.

blocks.text: וּבְתוֹרָתְךָ כָּתוּב לֵאמֹר שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל יְיָ אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ יְיָ אֶחָד׃

אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ. מְלוֹךְ עַל כָּל־הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בִּכְבוֹדֶֽךָ וְהִנָּשֵׂא עַל כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ בִּיקָרֶֽךָ וְהוֹפַע בַּהֲדַר גְּאוֹן עֻזֶּֽךָ עַל כָּל־יוֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל אַרְצֶֽךָ. וְיֵדַע כָּל־פָּעוּל כִּי אַתָּה פְּעַלְתּוֹ וְיָבִין כָּל־יָצוּר כִּי אַתָּה יְצַרְתּוֹ וְיֹאמַר
uncertainties: This block is a new indented paragraph. It runs on to the next Hebrew page.
The metegs are uncertain throughout. I can't tell whether פְּעַלְתּוֹ has a dagesh (פְּ or פְ).

blocks.text: Thee every knee should bow and every tongue swear. Before Thee, O Lord our God, will they kneel and fall and to the glory of Thy Name will they grant honour and they will all accept the yoke of Thy Kingdom. And Thou shalt soon reign over them for ever and ever. For Thine is the Kingdom and for all eternity shalt Thou reign in glory as it is written in Thy Torah: 'The Lord will reign for ever and ever'.
uncertainties: This block continues from the previous page.
The quoted verse is Exodus 15:18. I've left it inside the prayer block because it is embedded in a running paragraph.

blocks.text: And it was said: 'And He observed no wrong in Jacob nor did He see trouble in Israel, the Lord His God is with him and the royal Teruah within him.' And it was said: 'And He became King in Yeshurun when the heads of the people assembled together with the tribes of Israel'. And in Thy holy words it is written saying: 'For dominion is the Lord's and He is ruler over nations'. And it was said: 'The Lord has reigned, clothed in majesty, the Lord has clothed Himself in strength. He has girded Himself, the world is firmly founded, it does not totter.' And it was said: 'Lift up your heads, O gates and lift yourselves up, O portals of eternity, so that the King of glory may enter. Who is this King of glory? He is the Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in war. Lift up your heads, O gates, lift up, O portals of eternity, so that the King of glory may enter. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of Hosts, He is the King of glory, Selah'. And through Thy servants the prophets it is written saying: 'Thus says the Lord, the King of Israel and its redeemer, the Lord of Hosts: I am the first and I am the last and apart from Me there is no God'. And it was said: 'Deliverers shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau and dominion shall be the Lord's'. And it was said: 'And the Lord shall be King over all the earth, on that day will the Lord be One and His Name One'. And in Thy Torah it is written saying: 'Hear, O Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One'.
uncertainties: "redeemer" is hyphenated across a line break (re-/deemer) and "Deliverers" is hyphenated as Deliv-/erers. I have joined both.
The 'w' in "it was said" (before 'The Lord has reigned') has a speck above it in the image. This looks like a print artifact.
The English renders the verses in one continuous paragraph, so I haven't split it into separate citation blocks.
This is an abbreviation for אלהינו ואלהי אבותינו.

blocks.text: Our God and God of our fathers, reign over the whole world in Thy glory and rise above the whole earth in Thy grandeur. Shine forth in the exalted beauty of Thy might upon all the inhabitants of the territory of Thine earth so that every creature may recognize that Thou hast created it
uncertainties: The bottom line is slightly clipped in the scan, but it reads "every", "may" and "recognize". The sentence continues on the next page.

notes: I read both full pages and all four s208 bands. For s209 I read only band 4; the English on the full s209 page was clear, and band 4 shows nothing below the last line.
Neither page has rubrics, Shabbat additions, shofar-sound sequences, footnotes, German instructions or cantillation beyond the occasional meteg or accent marks noted above.
The verse quotations (Malkhuyot) are given as separate citation blocks. Each one starts with its connecting formula (וְנֶאֱמַר / וּבְדִבְרֵי… / וְעַל יְדֵי… / וּבְתוֹרָתְךָ…), as printed.
The four bands overlap. Where a line appeared in two bands, I counted it once.
The printed page number on both scans is 94: s208 is the Hebrew page and s209 is the English page facing it.
